rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the corollary after “Pour qu’un foncteur k-Alg → (Ens)”, the next line plainly reads “soit un faisceau”: the initial f has a tall crossing stem and descending hook, followed by the visible aisceau sequence. This first faisceau is not cancelled. A second faisceau remains in the following condition after the local deletions and insertion “ce soit” (crops/161-4_scan017_L1147.jpg).
rows.note: Keep the first “faisceau” as written. “Représentable (un schéma)” is the supplied mathematical repair of the author’s statement, not what the ink says at the disputed word. The actual original already preserves the local changes around the second occurrence. No representability criterion or circularity argument was independently proved.

events.type: used and rechecked in this run
events.outcome: Compared the actual original corollary against the enlarged first and second faisceau occurrences. The first is literally written and uncancelled, so it is preserved; no mathematical criterion was checked.
